caption: Figure 6. Amount of training data vs. mean Average Precision (mAP) on the val set of nuScenes. The dashed black line corresponds to the amount of training data in KITTI [32].
description:
Figure: Line graph showing the relationship between the amount of training data used and mean Average Precision (mAP) on the validation set of nuScenes. Three series are plotted: SSD+3D, PointPillars, and OFT. The SSD+3D series is highest, followed by PointPillars, and OFT is the lowest. The dashed black line represents the amount of training data in KITTI.

Text in figure: SSD+3D, PointPillars, OFT, mAP (%), % Training data used, KITTI.

caption: Figure 7. Average precision vs. matching function. CD: Center distance. IOU: Intersection over union. We use IOU = 0 . 7 for car and IOU = 0 . 5 for pedestrian and bicycle following KITTI [32]. We use CD = 2 m for the TP metrics in Section 3.1.
description:
This figure is a bar chart comparing the average precision (AP) of different matching functions for three object types: car, pedestrian, and bicycle. The chart shows AP percentages for four matching functions: Megvii, PointPillars, MonoDIS, and OFT. For cars, Megvii has the highest AP at 80%, followed by PointPillars at 70%. For pedestrians, Megvii also leads with 80%, while for bicycles, Megvii has the lowest AP at 20%.

Text in figure: Car, Pedestrian, Bicycle, Megvii, PointPillars, MonoDIS, OFT, CD, IOU, AP (%), 80, 60, 40, 20, 0.

caption: Figure 8. Top: Number of annotations per category. Bottom: Attributes distribution for selected categories. Cars and adults are the most frequent categories in our dataset, while ambulance is the least frequent. The attribute plot also shows some expected patterns: construction vehicles are rarely moving, pedestrians are rarely sitting while buses are commonly moving.
description:
This figure contains two bar charts. The top chart shows the number of annotations per category, with cars and adults being the most frequent categories and ambulance being the least frequent. The bottom chart shows the attribute distribution for selected categories, with construction vehicles rarely moving, pedestrians rarely sitting, and buses commonly moving.

Description: The top chart has parked cars as the highest series, followed by stopped cars, moving cars, and so on. The bottom chart shows various attributes for selected categories, with parked cars being the highest series and ambulance being the lowest.

This figure is a visual representation of a scene reconstruction using LiDAR points and camera images. It shows two panels: the left panel displays a 3D reconstruction of a scene with a bridge and surrounding environment, while the right panel shows a 2D projection of LiDAR points overlaid with color from the camera images. The reconstruction highlights the integration of LiDAR and camera data to create a detailed scene representation.

caption: Figure 16. PointPillars [51] detection performance vs. semantic prior map location on the val set. For the best lidar network (10 lidar sweeps with ImageNet pretraining), the predictions and ground truth annotations were only included if within a given distance of the semantic prior map.
description:
Description: This plot shows the Average Precision (AP) of various object detections against the distance from the semantic prior map. The series with the highest AP is 'car', maintaining around 0.7, while 'construction_vehicle' has the lowest AP, starting around 0.1. The plot includes series for 'car', 'truck', 'bus', 'trailer', 'pedestrian', 'motorcycle', 'bicycle', 'traffic_cone', and 'barrier'.

caption: Figure 17. Per class results for PointPillars on the nuScenes test set taken from the detection leaderboard.
description:
This figure is a collection of line graphs showing the recall versus precision and recall versus error for different object classes in the nuScenes dataset. Each graph represents a different object class, such as Car, Construction Vehicle, Pedestrian, Bicycle, and Barrier. The series in each graph are labeled with various detection methods and their performance metrics. The highest series in each graph is typically the one with the best performance, while the lowest series shows the worst performance. The figure provides a detailed comparison of the performance of different detection methods across various object classes.

Legend entries include: Dist, Scale, Orient, Vel, Attn, and various metrics like AP, IoU, and IoU. Axis titles are "Recall" and "Precision" or "Error".
